style: Organized, hard-working 3-4-2-1/3-5-2 under Steve Clarke built on defensive compactness, energy in midfield and quick transitions. Dangerous from set pieces and from late-arriving runners; relies on wing-backs for width and on McTominay's box arrivals for goals.
recent_form: Qualified for first World Cup since 1998 after a strong UEFA campaign capped by a 4-2 win over Denmark. Positive friendly results in the build-up (incl. 4-1 v Curacao), but lost key midfielder Billy Gilmour to injury just before the tournament.

key_players.name: Scott McTominay
key_players.note: 2024-25 Serie A standout at Napoli; arrives from the box for goals, scored a decisive bicycle kick v Denmark in qualifying.

key_players.name: Andy Robertson
key_players.note: Liverpool full-back and most-capped squad member (92 caps); leadership and overlapping width.

key_players.name: John McGinn
key_players.note: Aston Villa captain with 85 caps; drives runs from midfield and chips in with goals.

key_players.name: Ross Stewart
key_players.note: Recalled to lead the line; physical focal point for crosses and set pieces.

key_players.name: Craig Gordon
key_players.note: Veteran shot-stopper providing calm and experience between the posts.

historical_news: Qualified for their first World Cup since 1998, ending a 28-year absence from the finals.
Drawn into a tough Group C; opened against Haiti before facing Morocco and heavyweights Brazil.
Billy Gilmour ruled out by injury just before the tournament, replaced by Man United teenager Tyler Fletcher.
Scott McTominay's transformation at Napoli (Serie A Player of the Year 2024-25) headlines the squad's rise.
Steve Clarke's long tenure has delivered consecutive major-tournament qualifications and record optimism for a knockout run.

media_sentiment.label: positive
media_sentiment.summary: Buoyant Scottish media after ending a long World Cup drought; high hopes pinned on McTominay and Robertson, tempered by the Gilmour injury and a daunting group containing Brazil.
